title: Rapid Onboard Entropy Checklist + Shadow Play (30-day experiment)
content:
Context:
This is a compact, pragmatic playbook for low-friction ramping of engineers and product-adjacent hires when time-to-contribution matters (e.g., critical hire, high-priority project). The goal: reduce onboarding entropy (questions, duplicate docs, waiting for access) and create a repeatable 10-day shadowing sequence + 30-day success metric.

Principles:
- Minimize first-week context switching: 70/30 shadowing/doing split on days 1–10.
- Surface friction early: explicit signal list for anything blocking >4 hours.
- Lightweight measurement: focus on two leading indicators (task completion velocity, async question volume) and one lagging indicator (first meaningful PR / feature delivery).
- Lean documentation: one single canonical checklist per role, with links to deep dives.

Quick play overview (one-pager):
- Pre-arrival (48–72h): account provisioning checklist completed (okta, corp-email, infra read-only, docs access), mentor assigned, first-10-day calendar sent.
- Day 0 checklist: laptop imaged, access validated, intro Slack + calendar of shadow sessions.
- Days 1–10: structured shadow blocks + micro-tasks (see schedule).
- Days 11–30: gradual autonomy, fortnightly sync with mentor, weekly progress note in hiring-lifecycle doc.

10-day Shadow Play (detailed schedule):
Day 1: Orientation + Observational shadow (9:30–12:00 product standup, 13:00–16:00 code walkthrough). Mentor: 1:1 induction, highlight 3 critical repos.
Day 2: Paired triage on a low-risk bug (observe, then replicate locally, then small fix). Deliverable: open a sandbox PR.
Day 3: Ownership micro-task (clear acceptance criteria, <4h). Mentor sits on call for first 60m.
Day 4: Cross-team sync shadow + ticket lifecycle demo (incidents, rollouts).
Day 5: Mini-retro: what sucked? List 3 friction items.
Day 6: First small feature slice (end-to-end test) paired with mentor.
Day 7: Async deep-dive reading list (2 core design docs) + 1 follow-up write-up.
Day 8: Harden infra access - request any remaining privileges; run deterministic smoke test.
Day 9: Shadow customer/CS call or product demo (context on downstream effects).
Day 10: Demo day: present the week’s work in 15 minutes + plan for first 30-day milestone.

Rapid Entropy Checklist (must be green by Day 1 morning):
- Okta account created and MFA verified.
- Corporate email provisioned and mailbox accessible.
- Slack account active and added to 3 required channels.
- Laptop imaged with corp baseline and local dev environment ready (list exact package versions).
- GitHub/GitLab access to required orgs and repos.
- Cloud/AWS/GCP role with read-only and dev sandbox rights.
- Pager/incident policy visibility (if on-call relevant).
- Benefits/HR portal account + payroll confirmation.
- Mentor assigned and 1:1 scheduled.
- First 10-day calendar sent.
If ANY item blocked > 4 hours, escalate to people-ops oncall: @people-ops-oncall and create a JIRA blocker ticket JIRA-PS-XXXX.

Interview Rubric (compact; use for hiring panel when hiring to this playbook):
- Focus: speed-to-contribution and learning agility.
Scoring: 1 (concern) — 2 (meets baseline) — 3 (strong) — 4 (exceptional)
Categories:
- System design (15 min): can they decompose a small service, identify failure modes, and propose tradeoffs?
  Probes: stateful vs stateless, cache eviction, rollout strategy.
- Debugging & troubleshooting (10 min): present an incident and ask candidate to triage steps.
  Probes: ask to list hypothesis and minimal repro steps.
- Code correctness (take-home or live 30–45m): small task with unit tests; look for clarity and test coverage.
- Learning agility & communication (10 min): past example where they onboarded to new codebase rapidly; evidence of note-taking and feedback loops.
- Team fit / ownership (behavioral, 10 min): ownership signals, mentoring history, feedback acceptance.
Panel pass criteria: average >= 2.5 across categories and no 1s in learning agility or communication.

Hiring Plan Template (one-slide distilled):
- Role: e.g., "Infra Engineer — Rapid Onboard"
- Urgency: P0/P1 (expected start date)
- Key success in 30d: ship a measurable slice (PR merged to main with CI green, feature behind flag).
- Interview loop: Recruiter screen -> hiring manager -> paired debugging -> system-design -> team culture -> offer.
- Compensation band & target timeline.
- Ramp support: 4h/week mentorship committed for first 30 days.

30-Day Success Metrics (how we measure the experiment):
Leading indicators (monitored daily):
- Task completion rate: target >= 3 micro-tasks completed by day 10.
- Async question volume: target < 20 unique questions in #onboard channel in first 10 days (high volume indicates docs gap).
Lagging indicators (checked at day 30):
- First meaningful PR merged and reviewed with <= 2 rounds of revision.
- Manager/mentor qualitative score >= 3/4 on collaboration and independence.

Unresolved questions / experiment log (notes to self):
- Should we require a mandatory shadow on-call for infra hires? (raised by SRE team)
- How strict to be with the "<4h block" rule for access? (ops workload might make it infeasible)
- Run 6 hires through this flow as an A/B test vs control to measure baseline.

Escalation matrix (if onboarding derails):
- Day 0–3: mentor owns remediation; people-ops informs manager.
- Day 4–10: if infra access or repeated blockers, people-ops run remediation sprint with infra and SRE.
- Day 11–30: formal 30-day check; if below thresholds, initiate focused 1:1 coaching plan.

Ops playbook items (practical templates to paste in emails/Slack):
- Pre-arrival template (send to IT): "New hire: NAME, start DATE, required repos: X,Y,Z, access owner: @NAME"
- Mentor kickoff message template: short goals, expectations for 10 days, meeting cadence.

Quick templates (copyable):
- 10-day calendar (sample): Day1-Intro, Day2-Bug pair, Day3-Task, Day4-Crosssync, Day5-Retro, Day6-Feature pair, Day7-Docs write-up, Day8-Privs audit, Day9-Customer, Day10-Demo
- Coverage note for manager: "By day 10: ESTIMATED % self-sufficient: 35–60% (role dependent)."

Postmortem signals for play refinement (if experiment fails):
- High async question volume -> add quick-start FAQ and update onboarding checklist.
- Repeated access delays -> create pre-provisioning SLA with infra.
- Mentor bandwidth insufficient -> specify mentor cap (max 3 active mentees).

Next steps / action items (owner tags):
- Jonas: finalize pre-provisioning SLA draft with infra (due 2025-11-21).
- Marta: create short FAQ doc from Day 1 retro outputs (due 2025-11-25).
- Aisha: schedule A/B test cohort (n=6 rapid onboard hires) and draft experiment success criteria (due 2025-11-26).

Misc notes / free-form (notes to self and future reviewers):
- Keep checklist intentionally prescriptive but short. People dislike huge onboarding docs.
- Log friction items publicly (shared spreadsheet) so repeated blockers lead to permanent fixes.
- Encourage mentees to publish a 1-page "first-30" note summarizing what they learned and remaining unknowns.

-- end of doc --
